To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have prepared surface-modified hemispheres of polybutyl methacrylic acid/polybutylmethacrylate composite morphology by a one-step polymerization within polystyrene templates.
the composite particles can be surface-modified with a water-soluable vinylic monomers, such as acryl amide, by carrying out a swelling and polymerization procedure in the presence of this monomer.
the hemispheres are composed of a core of polystyrene and an exterior layer of poly(n-butyl-methacrylate).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the preparation, characterization, and surface modification of hemispherical polysterene/polybutylmethacrylate composite microspheres.
the synthesis, characterization, and selective surface functionalization of micrometer-sized polystylrene/poly(n-buthyl methacryate) composite particles of hemispherical shape.
the development of a novel process for the preparation of surface-modified composite particles of controlled size and shape.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

a surface-modified hemispheric polymer composite particle has been synthesized by a simple and straightforward process of single-step polymerization of the monomer butyl methacryl ate in the presence of the initiator benzoy peroxide within a uniform template microsphere.

the composite particles are composed of polystyrene cores, a poly(n-butyl) methacrylate shell, and a polyacrylamide surface layer, with the polyacrylamides being grafted onto the poly(n-butly methacrylate).
the surface-modification of the hemispherical composite particles is possible, but it is difficult to control the degree of modification.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

surface functionalization of polystyrene microspheres with a water-soluable monomer can be achieved by swelling and polymerization within the microspheres in the presence of the water-soluble monomer.
the surface of the composite particles could be modified with a thin layer of polyacrylamide, while the core was still polystyrene and the shell poly(n-butylmethacrylate).

a single-step swelling of polystyrene particles with a monomer solution containing a co-swelling agent, followed by in situ polymerization within the template microsphere, is an efficient method to prepare composite particles with a core-shell morphology.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the surface modification can be performed with high selectivity and control, resulting in a surface that is chemically different from the bulk of the particle.
the surface of a polymer composite particle with a hemispherical shape and narrow size distribution can be selectively modified by a surface-initiated polymerization process.
the composite particle surface can be modified by a second polymerization step in a manner which is selective to the surface.
